> **Lens**: Hold a user-facing page to the tooling a page of that quality is built with.
> Let the build, not the runtime, carry the dependencies.

## Relates to

- Extends [ADR-0020](0020-captured-report-is-a-static-microsite.md) (the record's status line says "refines")
- Extends [ADR-0021](0021-metric-names-carry-unit-and-provenance.md) (the record's status line says "refines")
- Extends [ADR-0024](0024-context-window-metrics-injected-messages-and-design-tokens.md) (the record's status line says "refines")
- Extends [ADR-0003](0003-runresult-is-a-stdlib-dataclass.md) (the record's status line says it "keeps" 0003's zero-runtime-dependency rule)

## Problem

### Symptom

`assets/report.html` grew to 870 lines of hand-written HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in one file.
It held a component library built from template strings, a hash router, two chart axes, a record-card renderer and the theme plumbing.
Plotly and highlight.js were pulled from a CDN at view time.
It works, and 0021's named ids and glossary keep it legible.
But every change is made without types, without a test runner that can mount a component, and without a formatter.
There is also no way to see the page against real data, short of re-running a sweep or a replay.

### Pain point

Composing a table by concatenating strings is how the `total_tokens` / `context %` columns came to sit beside each other and read as one quantity.

## Decision

### The lens

- **Given**: The bar the report is held to is a polished single-page application.
  The tools that produce those are well known.
  They are a typed component model, a design-system component library, a bundler, a unit-test runner that renders components, a linter and a formatter.
  None of them may become a runtime dependency of the Python package (0003).
  The page must still be one static file that `report.py` copies beside the captured JSON.
  It fetches from there or is populated inline, and is themed by `report.tokens.json` (0020, 0024).
- **We prefer**: A `report-ui/` bun workspace whose build emits one self-contained file, over hand-written HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in a single committed asset.
- **Because**: The build, not the runtime, then carries the dependencies: bun is needed to change the page, never to use the plugin.
- **Unless**: parity with the legacy page is not yet reached, in which case `assets/report.html` stays the legacy page and `ui-promote` is not run.

### In practice

- The page is authored in `report-ui/`, a bun workspace.
  It uses Vite, React, TypeScript in strict mode, Tailwind and shadcn/ui components, Vitest with Testing Library, ESLint and Prettier.
  `bun run build` emits **one** self-contained `dist/index.html`, with every script, style and font inlined by `vite-plugin-singlefile`.
  Nothing is fetched from a CDN at view time any more.
  The built file is promoted into `src/pytest_xharness_eval/assets/report.html` with `make ui-promote`, and committed.
  The Python package therefore ships a plain asset and keeps zero runtime dependencies.
  bun is needed to change the page, never to use the plugin.
- Three contracts from the first microsite are kept, so `report.py` does not change.
  The first is the `<!--XHARNESS_INLINE_DATA-->` marker at the top of `<head>`.
  The second is the `window.__XH_DATA__` inline payload, as the alternative to fetching `index.json`, `*.result.json`, `*.jsonl` and `report.tokens.json` from beside the page.
  The third is the `#session/<id>[/turn/<n>]` hash routes.
  The element ids and names of 0021's glossary are the component names, so `SessionTable` is `<SessionTable>`.
  A new panel gets its id, its glossary row and its component in the same change.
- Design tokens theme shadcn.
  `applyTokens` writes every token as an `--xh-*` custom property at runtime.
  `index.css` aliases shadcn's semantic variables to them, such as `--background`, `--primary` and `--chart-1`.
  A project's `xharness_report_design_tokens` file therefore restyles every component without a rebuild.
- Development is against real data.
  `make ui-dev CAPTURED=<skill>/evals/captured` serves the captured directory under the Vite dev server.
  `make ui-smoke CAPTURED=…` builds the page and populates it through `report.inline_page`, the same code path as `--xharness-report-inline`.
  It then renders the page headlessly in jsdom, printing the rows it mounted.
  There are no fixture JSONs for the page to drift from.
- The move is panel by panel.
  This record lands the workspace, the contracts, the theming, `ReportHeader`, `SweepOverview` with `SessionTable`, and `SessionView` with `SessionMetaTable`.
  Still on the legacy template, and moved in later changes: `TokenAccumulationChart`.
  Also the per-session charts `ContextWindowChart`, `TokenWaterfallChart`, `TurnTiersChart`, `OutputPerTurnChart` and `ChartAxisToggle`.
  Also `SessionTurnTable` and `TurnRawRecords` with the record-card component library, `SkillCoveragePanel`, `RecordKindsPanel`, `CostByTierPanel`, `ReconciliationPanel` and `FinalMessagePanel`.
  Charts will use shadcn's chart components over Recharts, replacing Plotly.
  Until parity, `assets/report.html` stays the legacy page and `ui-promote` is not run.

## Consequences

### Pros

- A contributor changing the page needs bun; one changing the plugin does not.
- CI type-checks, lints, tests and builds the workspace on every push now.
  Once the page is promoted, the same job rebuilds it and fails on a difference from the committed asset.
  The two therefore cannot drift.

### Cons

- The built page is a ~330 kB committed artifact that changes on every UI change, which is the price of a dependency-free wheel.
- `src/components/ui/` is shadcn's generated code and is excluded from lint and format.
  The root `.gitignore`'s Python patterns (`lib/`, `dist/`) are carved out for `report-ui/src/lib/`.
- While the move is in progress the two pages coexist; nothing a user sees changes until promotion.
